reason: The fibroblast conditions specify a route from stem-cell descendants to connective-tissue cells, which may make the supporting material.
expectation: A subset of the stem-cell population will differentiate into fibroblasts.

alternatives.reason: The muscle branch is also a goal and could be started first.

effect: The fibroblast branch now has collagen RNA messages while the unspecialized population remains available for the muscle branch.
reaction: The link between unchanged DNA and selective collagen gene activity is clear.
reason: The collagen messages and amino-acid supply suggest making collagen protein next.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids and collagen messages to make a collagen precursor.

alternatives.reason: I could prepare the separate muscle lineage first.

effect: The fibroblasts now contain processed collagen precursors in secretory vesicles, ready for the extracellular stage.
reaction: The connection from collagen RNA to secretion is clear.
reason: The extracellular fluid contains processing enzymes and space outside the cells, making it the likely next location for the collagen precursors.
expectation: The fibroblasts will secrete collagen precursors for extracellular processing into supporting material.

alternatives.reason: The separate muscle branch could also be started now.

effect: The collagen precursors were secreted and assembled into extracellular matrix, completing the supporting-material goal.
reaction: The distinction between living cells and the material they secrete is useful.
reason: The remaining goal calls for muscle-forming cells, and the muscle differentiation conditions specify that route for stem-cell descendants.
expectation: A separate subset of descendants will develop into muscle precursors.

effect: The muscle branch now has committed cells with muscle-protein RNA messages, but no mature fibres.
reaction: The parallel with collagen gene expression is clear.
reason: The muscle messages and shared amino-acid supply suggest making muscle proteins next.
expectation: The cells will use the messages and amino acids to produce muscle proteins and advance toward muscle precursors.

effect: The muscle-lineage cells used their RNA messages and amino acids to make muscle proteins, producing separate myoblasts and completing the chapter's goals. They are not yet mature muscle fibres.
reaction: The explicit distinction between precursors and fused muscle fibres is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making collagen-rich extracellular matrix was most worthwhile: the planned sequence connects protein production and secretion to the material supporting cells, clarifying that tissue includes extracellular surroundings.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second lineage repeated the message-to-protein pattern already established by the fibroblast branch. The parallel was instructive, but less surprising.

surprise.text: The muscle precursors already contain actin and myosin but remain separate, single-nucleus cells rather than mature fused fibres.

arbitrary.text: The differentiation conditions have a clear purpose, but their particular signals and how they change gene activity are not explained; the timed conditions function as a broad developmental shortcut.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how these precursors develop into muscle and how their structures relate to function, especially since this chapter stops before mature fibres form.
